questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating the Definite Integral of a Polynomial Function
questions.worked_solution:
Taking the antiderivative and evaluating the difference at the bounds, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{3}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{{x}^{3+1}}{3+1}{|}_{1}^{3} \\  & =\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}{|}_{1}^{3} \\  & =\frac{{3}^{4}}{4}-\frac{{1}^{4}}{4} \\  & =\frac{81}{4}-\frac{1}{4} \\  & =\frac{80}{4} \\  & =20.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating the Definite Integral of a Rational Function
questions.worked_solution:
Taking the antiderivative and evaluating the difference at the bounds, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{3}{x}^{-3}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{{x}^{-3+1}}{-3+1}{|}_{1}^{3} \\  & =\frac{{x}^{-2}}{-2}{|}_{1}^{3} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2{x}^{2}}{|}_{1}^{3} \\  & =-(\frac{1}{2\cdot {3}^{2}}-\frac{1}{2\cdot {1}^{2}}) \\  & =-(\frac{1}{18}-\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{4}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating the Definite Integral of a Rational Function
questions.worked_solution:
Taking the antiderivative and evaluating the difference at the bounds, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{-4}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{{x}^{-4+1}}{-4+1}{|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{{x}^{-3}}{(-3)}{|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{3{x}^{3}}{|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}(\frac{1}{{2}^{3}}-\frac{1}{{1}^{3}}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}(\frac{1}{8}-1) \\  & =\frac{7}{24}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating the Definite Integral of a Radical Function
questions.worked_solution:
Taking the antiderivative and evaluating the difference at the bounds, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{16}\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{16}{x}^{-2/3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{-2/3+1}}{(-\frac{2}{3}+1)}{|}_{1}^{16} \\  & =3\,{x}^{1/3}{|}_{1}^{16} \\  & =3\,\sqrt[3]{x}{|}_{1}^{16} \\  & =3(\sqrt[3]{16}-\sqrt[3]{1}) \\  & =3(2\sqrt[3]{2}-1).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating the Definite Integral of a Radical Function
questions.worked_solution:
Taking the antiderivative and evaluating the difference at the bounds, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{{x}^{4}}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{x}^{-4/3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{-4/3+1}}{-\frac{4}{3}+1}{|}_{1}^{3} \\  & =-3{x}^{-1/3}{|}_{1}^{3} \\  & =-3\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{x}}{|}_{1}^{3} \\  & =-3(\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{3}}-\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{1}}) \\  & =3(1-\frac{1}{\sqrt[3]{3}}) \\  & =3-\frac{3}{\sqrt[3]{3}} \\  & =3-\sqrt[3]{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Evaluating the Definite Integral of a Polynomial Function
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Taking the antiderivative and evaluating the difference at the bounds, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{4}x\,\text{d}x & =\frac{{x}^{1+1}}{1+1}{|}_{0}^{4} \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}{|}_{0}^{4} \\  & =\frac{{4}^{2}}{2}-\frac{{0}^{2}}{2} \\  & =\frac{16}{2} \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Evaluating the Definite Integral of a Rational Function
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Taking the antiderivative and evaluating the difference at the bounds, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{-3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{-3+1}}{-3+1}{|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =-\frac{{x}^{-2}}{2}{|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}({2}^{-2}-{1}^{-2}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{4}-1) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}(-\frac{3}{4}) \\  & =\frac{3}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Evaluating the Definite Integral of a Radical Function
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Taking the antiderivative and evaluating the difference at the bounds, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{4}\sqrt{x}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{4}{x}^{1/2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{2}{3}{x}^{3/2}{|}_{1}^{4} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}({4}^{3/2}-{1}^{3/2}) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(\sqrt{64}-1) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(8-1) \\  & =\frac{14}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
